newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins ease with Bradys, good support seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins ease with Bradys, good support seen.

text.p: Russian MinFins eased further on Friday following the global Brady trend but dealers said MinFins were otherwise finding firm support on the absence of bad news from Russia and ahead of the forthcoming Eurobond.
A senior Deutsche Bank AG official said on Friday Russia would issue its second Eurobond for as much as two billion marks ($1.18 billion) by the end of next week.

Dealers said no straight impact had been seen on the market of the news but, together with Russia's 1997 state budget approved by President Boris Yeltsin this week, it contributed to the positive attitude towards Russia.
"MinFins are following the general emerging market trend which started on Wednesday," one dealer said.
Prices of U.S. Treasuries and Bradys started to go down on Wednesday after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's inflation warning pointing to higher interest rates.
"The market was going down in line with other papers but it has good support as we have no negative news. People were just levelling their positions," an International Moscow Bank dealer said.
Dealers said support levels for the most liquid fourth, fifth and seventh tranches were 63.00, 44.50 and 38.50 respectively.
